children: Cars are getting smarter, using software to control more functions. That dynamic is driving growth at BlackBerry, the company once known for pioneering handheld devices.
BlackBerry reported fiscal second-quarter earnings per share of 7 cents from sales of $163.3 million. Wall Street was looking for 4 cents and $142.5 million, respectively.
A year ago, BlackBerry reported profit of 4 cents a share and sales of $129.6 million. Sales grew 26% year over year.
"Our strong second-quarter performance provides further evidence that BlackBerry's profitable growth model is working," said CEO John Giamatteo in a news release.
BlackBerry doesn't make hardware anymore. Its QNX operating system is embedded in roughly 275 million cars, providing auto makers with a platform to build applications.

"QNX delivered record performance in the quarter, driven by strength in our core automotive business," added Giamatteo. Revenue increased to $80.3 million, up 27% year over year. "As we enter the second half of the year, we remain focused on disciplined execution, investing behind our growth opportunities."

BlackBerry also said its Alloy Kore middleware software platform received its first design win. That represents another software layer the company is supplying to the auto industry, which can turn into more revenue per car for BlackBerry.

Looking ahead, BlackBerry expects fiscal-third quarter sales of about $149 million and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Ebitda) of about $33 million. Wall Street projects $148 million and $34 million, respectively.

For fiscal 2027, BlackBerry expects revenue of roughly $626 million, up from $549 million in fiscal year 2026, and Ebitda of about $150 million. Wall Street projects $612 million and $138 million, respectively.

Numbers looked solid. BlackBerry stock was up 6% at $8.88 in premarket trading, shortly after results were released, while S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 0.5% and 0.3%, respectively.
Coming into Thursday, shares have gained 121% this year.
Business momentum has been accelerating. BlackBerry should generate fiscal 2007 sales of about $626 million. At the start of the fiscal year, analysts projected about $577 million.
Gains have left shares trading for about 32 times Ebitda expected over the coming 12 months, up from about 26 times a year ago.
